headline: High-risk git/workspace overlap: Aider can write and commit shared repo state while MinerU can ingest shared files via MCP/API, creating medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo; MinerU can consume local files and exposes an MCP Server. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if MinerU outputs are copied into the repo or routed through MCP, though no direct automatic bridge is documented.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are pasted into Aider-managed files or MCP messages without sanitization
IF Aider is configured to treat repository text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate staging directory
Require manual review before Aider edits any MinerU-generated text
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to copied document text
Use a dedicated repo branch for extracted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to MinerU outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider can read/write repository files and handles model-provider API keys via env vars; MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and similar files and exposes REST/FastAPI/MCP interfaces. If sensitive documents are placed in the shared workspace, both agents can touch them, creating a realistic leakage path through model/API calls and shared files.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in the shared repo or input directory
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external model/API backend
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside the shared workspace
Disable external model calls for sensitive runs
Use redacted copies for extraction and coding
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state in a shared git repo, while MinerU is read-only on filesystem but can operate concurrently through API/MCP. The main conflict is Aider mutating shared repo state while MinerU reads or processes related files, which can cause inconsistent outputs even without direct write-write contention.
conditions: IF MinerU reads files that Aider is actively rewriting
IF Aider commits while MinerU is extracting from the same working tree
mitigations: Serialize Aider edits and MinerU extraction jobs
Use separate working copies for each agent
Freeze the repo during extraction runs
Review git diffs before rerunning MinerU
requires-engineering: add lock coordination around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or repo changes, and MinerU can emit extracted text through API/MCP. If MinerU consumes Aider-produced artifacts or Aider consumes MinerU-extracted text without verification, errors can propagate into commits or downstream documents. No built-in verification or locking is documented in either profile, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF MinerU-derived text is used as authoritative input to Aider
IF Aider commits changes based on unverified MinerU extraction
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Compare extracted text against source documents
Keep generated artifacts separate from source files
Add checksum checks for extracted outputs
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is open-source and runs as the user with git-repo access; MinerU is open-source and documented as private/fully offline. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident: shared repository handling of potentially sensitive source code or documents may conflict with local retention expectations.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository or input directory
IF local retention/deletion requirements are stricter than the repo workflow
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared repo
Set short local retention windows
Document deletion/export procedures
Use synthetic or anonymized test data
requires-engineering: add policy-aware retention controls
